questions.question: In story S20 (Privacy invariant harness across flows), is there any vacuous or placeholder production path: a no-op/stub body, a tautological assertion, a frozen stand-in constant, or an optional dependency (injected port, handler, client handle) that silently degrades to non-behavior when not injected? Cite file:line for each injection point in app/tests/unit/marmot/privacy.harness.test.ts; app/tests/unit/marmot/helpers/recordingTransport.ts and show that omitting the dependency fails loudly rather than succeeding silently.

Could `client` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md (imports only via each module's index.ts, no React-context imports under app/src/lib/marmot/**, no ts-mls or @internet-privacy/marmot-ts imports)?

Does S20 comply with the architecture.md boundary rules: only `client/` constructs or disposes the MarmotClient, code inside HistoryBackend calls / inbox handlers / client listeners never awaits an account-scope client call (follow-up work via the owned setTimeout(0) FIFO), group sender identity comes only from orderingKey.account, and idb-keyval update() is not used? List each rule touched by this story's files with file:line evidence, or state why it is not touched.

Do unit, property, and (where the AC names them) library-harness or e2e tests cover the artifacts named in S20's scope (app/tests/unit/marmot/privacy.harness.test.ts; app/tests/unit/marmot/helpers/recordingTransport.ts)? Show that tests use real collaborators or test fixtures rather than mocking the helper used at the SUT call site, that idb mocks are seeded out of key order where order matters, and that at least one test fails if the production code is replaced by a no-op.

Does the delivered S20 implementation match the intent of its scope (Recording-transport library harness across create, invite, accept, send, join request and profile exchange: no kind 0, no profile strings outside 1059/445, 30443/10050/30078 clean, invite-context only as a gift wrap.) and respect its exclusions (Production changes)? Identify any capability owned by a later story that was built ahead, or any in-scope capability left unimplemented.

Which trust or validation boundaries does S20 touch (signer budget/permissions, relay-supplied events, rumor sender/pubkey attribution, invite/join payloads, privacy invariant that no profile metadata is published to public relays)? Show the validation or defensive check at each boundary with file:line evidence and a test that feeds a malformed or hostile input and observes rejection.

AC-PRIV-1: With a recording transport, across create, invite, accept, send, join request and profile exchange, no published unwrapped event has kind 0, and no published event other than kinds 1059/445 contains the sender's nickname or avatar strings (substring scan over every published event's JSON). Events of kinds 30443, 10050 and 30078 MUST contain neither string. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [harness] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-PRIV-2: The invite-context rumor (AC-CTX-1) travels only as a kind-1059 gift wrap; the recording transport MUST see no published event of kind 21064 at top level. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [harness] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.
